title: The Chain Reaction Machine
subtitle: Cause & Effect — live with your Enrichment group

learningFocus.summary: Students practise identifying cause-and-effect relationships — a core reading-comprehension and reasoning skill that underpins understanding sequence, consequence and argument in every subject. Working live alongside their Enrichment group, they connect the concept to real choices in their own lives and celebrate each other's thinking with positive, teacher-safe reactions.

orient.objective: Today you will learn to spot a cause and its effect — and see how one effect can become the next cause.
orient.realLife: Every day you set off chains of cause and effect — pressing a button, being kind to a friend, forgetting your umbrella. Spotting the chain helps you guess what happens next.
orient.courseLink: This is today's Primary Enrichment English session — a live, playful practice of an idea that helps with reading, science and everyday decisions.
successCriteria: I can point to the cause and the effect in a short scene.
I can explain why understanding cause and effect is useful.
I can use cause and effect to guess what happens next in a new situation.

predict.prompt: Quick guess before we start: which one happens FIRST?

rounds.cause: You press the button on the remote control.
You water a seed every day and give it sunlight.
You say something kind to a friend.
You push the first domino in a long line.

options.label: All the dominoes fall, one after another.
The dominoes turn into a tower.

rounds.cause: You leave your umbrella at home on a rainy day.

options.label: You get wet on the way to school.

rounds.cause: You recycle a plastic bottle instead of throwing it in the bin.

options.label: Less plastic rubbish ends up in the ocean.

rounds.cause: You forget to water the class plant for two whole weeks.

options.label: The pot turns into a seed.

rounds.cause: You knock over the very first domino in a huge spiral.

options.label: The whole spiral falls in one long chain.
The dominoes all jump upright again.

explain.prompt: Why does understanding cause and effect actually help you in real life?

options.label: It helps you guess what might happen before you act.
It only matters in made-up stories.
It has nothing to do with real life.

apply.prompt: Your class plant looks droopy and sad. Which cause will fix it?

options.label: Water it and give it sunlight.
Put it in a dark cupboard.

knowledgeCheck.cause: You brush your teeth every morning and night.

knowledgeCheck.effect: You feel tired the next day.

knowledgeCheck.cause: You share your toys with a friend.
knowledgeCheck.effect: Your friend feels included and happy.

knowledgeCheck.cause: You practise a new skill every day.
knowledgeCheck.effect: You get better at it over time.

knowledgeCheck.cause: You leave ice cream out in the sun.
You forget to charge your tablet overnight.
knowledgeCheck.effect: The battery is empty in the morning.
